record.what_happened: Which Sounding Line branches deserve compute next: kill. Licensed by O02, O04, O07, O10, O16, I06, G01, G04, G05, G06, G13, G15, I07, I08, A01, A02, A03, A10, A12, A13, I05, C03, C04, C05, C07, C08, C14, C16, P01, P03, I03, A06, Q05, A07, H10, O07, P14, H06, H07, H10, H15, H03, H14, H03, H13, Q08, G04, G05, G07, G08, G09, G10, G12, G13, G16, A09, H13, H14, P14, O16, H03, H09, G01, A06, H13, P14; the transfer gap is every item's gap is inherited; this item only orders them.
record.what_changed_in_the_project_world: A text-side design is exported with its gap, its records, its baseline and its failure meaning attached; nothing here is human evidence.

hypothesis: Only validated, transferring, prediction-gated shapes are ranked for Sounding Line compute, with the controls each needs and the failure signatures to watch.

O02.what_happened: With the scalar total held fixed, the factored reader named the weighted dimension 79% of the time and predicted held-out choices +0.66 nats better than the total-cost reader.

O04.what_happened: One choice moved the posterior by near_tie 0.10, dominated 0.01, attractive 0.09, costly_chosen 0.15 nats; the shift tracked the counterfactual utility at rank correlation -0.36.

O07.what_happened: Imposed work gave the record reader 0.000 nats of preference evidence and the flag-blind reader 1.02; voluntary choices gave 0.85.

O10.what_happened: A reader scoring anticipated cost put the same mass on the truth whether the expenditure was chosen, sunk or discovered late (spread 0.000); a hindsight reader lost 0.01 of that mass when the cost was not the maker's decision.

O16.what_happened: Under missing and false alternatives the naive reader's calibration error was 0.17 against 0.16 for the reader that treated the menu as a claim.

I06.what_happened: Weighting each cost dimension alone shifted the choice distribution by time 0.154, execution 0.150, cognitive 0.155, epistemic 0.151, social 0.149, risk 0.145, imposed 0.465 (Jensen-Shannon); a classifier reading only total paid cost named the weighted dimension 17% of the time against 12% chance.

G01.what_happened: With twelve artifacts and their claims' truths, the reader named the maker's stance 85% of the time against 14% chance; a surface classifier on the artifacts named it 16%.

G04.what_happened: Reliability posterior against the planted rate: helpful_incompetent 0.93 vs 1.00, neutral_reliable 0.93 vs 1.00, adversarial_truthful 0.93 vs 1.00, helpful_outdated 0.59 vs 0.60.

G05.what_happened: Strong artifact evidence moved the content posterior +0.19 more than weak, whatever the history; a revealed history moved the reliability posterior +0.34 more than none, whatever the evidence.

G06.what_happened: Belief update moved +0.80 with the source's truthfulness and 0.0e+00 with its alignment; preference movement moved +0.64 with alignment.

G13.what_happened: A false note left 2% of the mass on the wrong side against strong contradicting evidence and 34% against weak; a reader that took the note as truth was wrong 100% of the time.

G15.what_happened: Every channel responded to its declared factors by at least 0.33 and to any other factor by at most 0.00.

I07.what_happened: A classifier on each artifact's token histogram, entropy, length and polish named the goal 18% of the time against 14% chance; a reader who learned the claims' truths named it 85% of the time. Across a source's artifacts, evidence one-sidedness identified goals 12% of the time.

I08.what_happened: Changing what a source asserts left the content posterior unmoved to 0.0e+00; changing the evidence tokens left the source posterior unmoved to 0.0e+00; changing relevance and alignment moved only the uptake channels.

A01.what_happened: At neutral settings both analogues reproduced the plain posterior to 0.0e+00; under budgets of one, two and four cue families their log scores differed by 0.20 nats on average.

A02.what_happened: With one cue family to inspect, learned selection bought +5.26 nats per unit cost more than random inspection and the oracle +5.33; salience-driven inspection scored -6.55 relative to learned.

A03.what_happened: On identical evidence, learned weights scored +14.10 nats over uniform and wrong weights -2.89; the wrong weighting was confidently wrong 26% of the time against 9%.

A10.what_happened: After the maker turned out to be the reader's opposite, the adaptive reader kept 0.03 of its mass on the reader's own profile against 0.04 for the fixed local reader and 0.04 for the broad one; it reallocated in 81% of streams.

A12.what_happened: Under adversarial salience the salience-driven reader lost 1.22 nats and scored 6.51 below a reader using learned cue reliability.

A13.what_happened: No policy gained more than -13.141 nats in a null world; counting the surface twice raised confidence by +0.20 with an accuracy change of +0.00, the planted failure.

I05.what_happened: Neutral attention reproduced the plain posterior to 0.0e+00; the largest gain any policy found in a no-information world was -11.294 nats, against +0.78 where channels carried information.

C03.what_happened: Knowing the maker's common substrate was worth -0.00 nats on its profile after one artifact against a prior spread over every family; the broad prior needed 1 artifacts to reach what the substrate prior had at one.

C04.what_happened: Against a non-self prior matched on entropy and on expected distance to the truth, the self prior scored +0.26 nats on the nearest makers, -0.16 on the farthest and +1.21 on planted anti-similar makers after one artifact; pooled over everything the difference was +0.31.

C05.what_happened: For readers typical of their substrate the self prior beat the common population prior by -0.75 nats after one artifact; for anti-similar readers it lost -0.81.

C07.what_happened: Using the maker's claimed group as a prior was worth +1.34 nats when the claim was true and the convention shared, and -24.53 when only the claim matched.

C08.what_happened: Practitioners predicted makers' method choices +0.04 nats better than novices and read profiles -0.33 better; readers who knew the templates but not the transitions gained +0.00 on methods.

C14.what_happened: On the maker's hidden next goal the self prior beat the equally local non-self prior by +0.04 nats for near makers and -0.03 for far makers; pooled, the difference was -0.00.

P01.what_happened: For far and anti-similar makers the self prior was corrected with a half-life of 5.9 artifacts to a residual self mass of 0.01, with an order effect of 7.5e-15; the equally local non-self prior corrected with a half-life of 6.2.

P03.what_happened: After three artifacts the reader kept 0.46 of its mass on its own profile when the maker really matched and 0.14 when the maker differed but a reliable-looking note said it matched, against 0.02 with no such note.

I03.what_happened: For every reader the equally local non-self prior matched the self prior's entropy to machine precision and its expected distance to the truth within 0.061 nats; the generic local prior within 0.003.

A06.what_happened: The best first cue for novices was random and for experts random; after every cue the posteriors agreed to within 0.00 nats regardless of entry.

Q05.what_happened: Adaptive readers opened with purpose 1% of the time as novices and 1% as experts, with mechanics first 0% of the time for experts; final posteriors converged.

A07.what_happened: Weighting the anomaly channel gained +0.31 nats on the maker's regime when mistakes were handled in regime-specific ways, -3.48 for forced defects with no handling, and +0.00 when nothing went wrong.

H10.what_happened: A model of how the controller handled each mistake predicted whether a revision followed +0.57 nats better than the revision frequency; corrected was revised 100%, accepted was revised 0%, exploited was revised 0%, concealed was revised 100%, missed was revised 0%.

P14.what_happened: On identical artifacts the reader's top regime mass was 0.50 (abstention); after the separating artifacts it was 0.97 where the alternative method was distinguishable (30720/130560 of pairs), 0.77 in the borderline band, and 0.55 where methods coincide.

H06.what_happened: Suppression and amplification routes were classified 100% and 75% of the time and the next intervention was predicted at a log score of -0.48 against -0.69 for a coin flip.

H07.what_happened: Across two directors and two domains, the correction route followed the subordinate's style in at least 84% of teams in every cell.

H15.what_happened: The graph model predicted the hidden next intervention at a log score of -1.08 against -0.98 for the best baseline.

H03.what_happened: Director versus shared brief: artifact-only 50%, coherence 50%, interaction records 100% against 50% chance.

H14.what_happened: Discrimination by record level: artifact 50%, timings 50%, proposals 50%, alternatives 50%, accept_veto 50%, role_map 47%, full_log 100%; the first level reaching 75% was full_log.

H13.what_happened: On artifacts that were literally the same, a classifier named the history 50% of the time against 50% chance, and the artifact-only reader's topology posterior stayed flat.

Q08.what_happened: Minimum discriminativeness by probe set: commission 0.007, channel 0.074, query 0.010; commissions differed pairwise by 0.288.

G07.what_happened: A high-trust default reached a reliable source's rate within 2 claims against 16 for a low default, and accepted 4.4 false assertions from an unreliable source against 0.2.

G08.what_happened: The best-predicting trust rule was stable: bayes, one_change: change_point, many_changes: change_point.

G09.what_happened: Learning from a later event that the source misleads raised the accuracy of its earlier ambiguous claims by +1.00; the same event from another source changed them by +0.00; a false revelation by +0.00.

G10.what_happened: Trust recovered by apology +0.00, costly_action +0.13, repeated_reliability +0.17, third_party +0.10, none +0.00 after three revealed false assertions.

G12.what_happened: Carrying a source's learned reliability improved truth reading by +0.39 in its own domain, -1.80 in a domain where it misleads, and -1.80 for a namesake.

A09.what_happened: With strong artifact evidence and a source whose history and assertions ran against the truth, the factored reader kept 83% of its mass on the truth against 73% for a single-trust-number reader; the content posterior never moved with the history.

H09.what_happened: With proposal records the private goal was recovered 97% of the time; without them the reader's top mass was 0.23, an abstention.

gates.detail: a task whose answer is known by construction returns that answer

gates_summary.how_to_read: a gate RECORDS here and does not raise, so an exploratory sweep is never killed mid-run. tests/test_gates.py walks every committed verdict and fails the suite on anything in failed_names or unexpected_passes, which puts the hard stop where a result would become public. THREE categories, and they are not the same thing: failed_names is a control that broke; documented_failures is a gate marked expected_to_fail, which records a KNOWN defect so the evidence travels with the result (S-2's dead manipulation, S-3's fitted threshold); unexpected_passes is a documented defect that has started passing, which means somebody fixed it without updating the gate and is the one nobody would otherwise notice. A skipped gate counts as passing but is reported separately: it means an optional dependency was absent, never that a check succeeded.
